scores.reason: Candidate 1 leads with pay figures that are not in the facts (no per-mile rate is given; facts show annual ranges and a $1,500 bonus). The card_get and headline invent a $0.72/mile and $5,000 sign-on that don't exist in the facts. Beyond the factual issue, it ignores team, dedicated, dry van, coast-to-coast, and home schedule entirely. Spanish is natural and mirrors the English well, but the core specifics are fabricated.

Candidate 2 is built almost entirely from filler: 'dynamic team,' 'competitive pay,' 'great freight,' 'family atmosphere,' 'exciting opportunity,' 'truly value our drivers.' The card_need and card_apply slots appear to be copies of card_get, which is a structural failure. The headline 'Great pay, great team' is pure filler. Spanish mirrors the English filler word for word.

Candidate 3 uses all three cards correctly and leads with real figures ($95K–$110K, drop and hook, late-model). card_need lists every stated requirement. The primary_text names Silvicom Inc, the lane (coast to coast), the team policy, and the $1,500 referral bonus. Spanish is natural, uses 'drop and hook' as trade term, and keeps miles in the correct unit. Minor weakness: 'steady lane' is slightly vague, but everything else is checkable.
